newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire parliament votes potential interim leader.
newsitem.headline: Zaire parliament votes potential interim leader.

text.p: Zairean lawmakers voted Archbishop Laurent Pasinya Monsengwo as speaker of the transition parliament on Saturday, making him a potential interim successor to President Mobutu Sese Seko, parliamentary spokesmen said.
"Monsengwo has just been voted by near unanimity as speaker of parliament," Christophe Lutundula, second deputy speaker of parliament from the moderate opposition, told Reuters.

"He is not an alternative to either President Mobutu or Kabila," Kutundula said, referring to rebel leader Laurent Kabila whose forces have seized most of Zaire and are closing in on the capital in a drive to topple Mobutu.
"We are hoping he will play a role as a national mediator and will persuade all sides to agree on a way of safeguarding the democratic process in Zaire," Lutundula added.
The vote, conducted by a show of hands, was marred by a prior walkout by the UDPS radical opposition party of Etienne Tshisekedi, and it was not clear whether a quorum was achieved.
